text:
matt: Heads-up — after yesterday's runtime kernel rollout I'm seeing a consistent bump in tail token latency for some routes. Need a quick way to tie token-level metrics back to the request traces so we can answer: was it kernel selection, batching, or KV cache misses?

tara: Ugh. Which routes? model-small? or the long-context customers?

matt: Mostly api/v1/generate for 8k sequences. P95 token-latency up ~30ms. cpu/gpu utilization normal. Batching profile looks weirder — more small batches.

john: If small batches increased, could be the new batching heuristic. Do we tag batch-size on the request span today?

leah: We have batch_size in aggregate metrics, but not per-request on traces. We only emit token breakdown counters with no request_id.

matt: Right — we need to emit an envelope per request that carries request_id + trace_id + chosen_kernel + selected_batch_hint + kv_hit_rate (sampled). Something lightweight.

devon: Agreed. Minimal change: add trace_id into the existing token-latency counter labels and emit a single JSON blob to the trace log when request finishes. Example line we started prototyping: ```{"req_id":"r_1234","trace_id":"t_abc","kernel":"matmul_v2","batch_size":3,"tokens":512,"kv_hits":0.86}```

aaron: That looks good. We should avoid high-cardinality labels in metrics; keep trace_id out of metrics ingestion pipeline. Instead put trace_id in the event log and link by request_id that exists in both metrics and traces.

matt: Good call. Proposal: metrics still have request_id (short hash), token-level buckets, kernel tag (coarse), and an event log line with trace_id + full metadata. Dashboard will resolve the request_id -> trace_id via the event log viewer.

tara: For observability: can we add a 'per-request breakdown' view that shows token timeline and the spans for kernel selection, batching wait, KV lookup, and token generation? We can stitch those if spans are emitted for each stage.

john: We already have spans for gen.start and gen.end. Need two more: kernel.pick and kv.lookup (sampled). kernel.pick should include selected kernel name and reason code (latency_est/cost_est).

leah: On sampling: kv.lookup span for every request is heavy. Proposal: sample at 10% + all requests with batch_size < 4 or tokens > 2048. That targets problematic cases.

matt: Sounds reasonable. Who can add the event-line and kernel.pick span? I can do the batching heuristic changes in the next PR.

devon: I can add kernel.pick span and the event log line in infra-runtime. Will push a small instrumentation patch: addTraceEvent(req) call before kernel selection and emit at finish.

aaron: Also add a unixts and seq index for token events to allow building the token timeline in the UI. Example event payload: ```
req_event = {
  "req_id": "r_1234",
  "trace_id": "t_abc",
  "ts": 1779001234,
  "token_index": 0,
  "stage": "kernel.pick",
  "attrs": {"kernel":"matmul_v2","reason":"latency_est"}
}
```

matt: Perfect. Once traces have kernel.pick + token events and the event log links req_id->trace_id we can build a per-request breakdown panel. Can the Console team wire it to the metrics explorer?

tara: Yep, UI work: a new panel that accepts req_id and pulls events + spans + metrics. Should show a stacked timeline: batching wait | kernel pick | kv lookup | token gen per-token. We'll expose a 'open trace in Jaeger' link too.

aaron: Quick perf note: if kernel selection is cheap (<1ms) but we see 20ms tail, likely batch waiting or KV misses. The token timeline will show waits between tokens.

leah: I'll add a small profiler dump to the infra artifact when a request exceeds p99: ```cmd
curl -s http://local-agent/debug/profile?req=r_1234 | jq .summary
# output: {"batch_wait_ms": 22, "kv_miss_count": 3, "kernel_select_ms": 0.8}
```

matt: Great. Timeline: instrumentation PRs this week, Console panel next sprint. For immediate triage, can someone run a few problematic req_ids and paste event logs?

devon: Running one now for r_ab12: ```
EVENT: {"req_id":"r_ab12","trace_id":"t_f00","ts":1779001250,"stage":"batch.wait","attrs":{"wait_ms":18}}
EVENT: {"req_id":"r_ab12","trace_id":"t_f00","ts":1779001268,"stage":"kernel.pick","attrs":{"kernel":"matmul_v2","reason":"quant_est"}}
EVENT: {"req_id":"r_ab12","trace_id":"t_f00","ts":1779001270,"stage":"kv.lookup","attrs":{"hits":0.0}}
```

matt: That one looks like batch waiting + kv miss. Thanks. If people can run a couple more and post, we'll decide whether to revert the kernel bump or tweak batching heuristic. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Deploy alert: infra-runtime/commit/ffa213 deployed to prod at 1779001220 by devon. No rollback detected.

tara: I'll coordinate with Console to reserve a dev env for the panel prototype.

john: I'll compare pre-rollout historic small-batch distribution vs post-rollout to quantify change. Pulling from metrics now.

matt: Awesome. Thanks y'all — keep posting noisy req_ids here. Small follow-up: let's avoid adding trace_id to long-term metrics to keep ingestion stable. Use short req_id in metrics and full trace_id only in event logs.

leah: noted. I'll open two PRs: one for event emission + spans, one for the p99 profiler hook.

matt: Perfect. Closing loop once we have enough examples to decide next action.
